items.title: This deep-sea enzyme survives heat that destroys most proteins
items.title_en: This deep-sea enzyme survives heat that destroys most proteins
items.title_zh: 这种深海酶能够耐受高温，而这种高温会破坏大多数蛋白质
items.summary_en: A deep-sea microbe uses an exceptionally heat-resistant enzyme to turn atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia at temperatures that would destroy most proteins. Its unusual structure and a newly observed reaction state may reveal an ancient, shared mechanism behind nitrogen fixation and could eventually inspire cleaner biotechnology and fertilizer production.
items.summary_zh: 一种深海微生物利用一种耐热性极强的酶，在足以破坏大多数蛋白质的温度下将大气中的氮转化为氨。该酶不同寻常的结构以及新观察到的反应状态，或许能揭示固氮作用背后一种古老的、共通的机制，并最终为开发更清洁的生物技术和化肥生产提供灵感。

items.title: Billions in rare earth elements may be hiding in America’s coal ash
items.title_en: Billions in rare earth elements may be hiding in America’s coal ash
items.title_zh: 美国煤灰中可能蕴藏着价值数十亿美元的稀土元素
items.summary_en: Scientists are looking to diatoms, sea sponges, and plants for a cleaner way to recover rare earth elements and other valuable minerals hidden inside coal ash, red mud, and mine tailings. The bio-inspired approach could turn massive industrial waste piles into useful materials while reducing energy use, harsh chemicals, and reliance on new mining.
items.summary_zh: 科学家们正从硅藻、海绵和植物中寻找更清洁的方法，以提取隐藏在煤灰、红泥和矿山尾矿中的稀土元素及其他有价值的矿物。这种受生物启发的方法不仅能将大量工业废料转化为有用材料，还能减少能源消耗、降低强腐蚀性化学品的用量，并减少对新矿开采的依赖。
